verdict: Corning's sales rose 18% to $4.9B and GAAP EPS rose 56% to $0.78 as data-center demand drove Optical Communications sales up 44% — Gen AI product sales more than doubled.

segments.name: Optical Communications
segments.note: Fiber, cable and connectivity for networks — enterprise networks grew 84% and Gen AI product sales more than doubled on data-center demand.

segments.name: Glass Innovations
segments.note: Display glass and specialty glass (including Gorilla Glass) — down 3%.

segments.name: Automotive, Solar, Life Sciences & other
segments.note: Automotive $470M (+4%), Solar $436M (+37%) and Life Sciences & Emerging Growth $290M (+1%), less $226M of corporate and elimination items so the segments foot to total sales.

opex.name: Research, development & engineering
opex.note: Research, development and engineering — Corning's innovation engine.

opex.name: Amortization of purchased intangibles
opex.note: Amortization of intangibles bought in acquisitions.

otherDetail: A $138M gain on translated earnings contracts (currency hedges) and $17M of interest income, less $87M of interest expense and $11M of other expense — a net $57M boost.
footerNote: Net income in the chart is the total of $746M; $680M was attributable to Corning and $66M to non-controlling interests. Segment sales are Corning's reported segment figures; the third chart segment groups Automotive, Solar and Life Sciences & Emerging Growth Businesses net of corporate/elimination items (-$226M) so the pieces foot to total net sales.

takeaways.title: AI data centers are buying the fiber
takeaways.text: Optical Communications sales rose 44% to $2.38B and its net income rose 80% to $532M. Enterprise Networks grew 84%, with Gen AI product sales up more than 100% — outpacing GPU unit growth, Corning says.

takeaways.title: Solar is the second growth leg
takeaways.text: Solar sales grew 37% to $436M as U.S. production ramped (more slowly than planned) and new U.S. trade action on solar imports helped pricing; the segment was roughly breakeven (-$7M).

takeaways.title: Core EPS vs $0.78 GAAP
takeaways.text: Core EPS of $0.91 rose 36%; the GAAP figure of $0.78 (+56%) includes items Corning excludes from 'core', and the quarter's other income includes a $138M currency-contract gain.
